store.name: Store
store.lead: Every app built on the Harith Kavish ecosystem, packaged and ready to install.

apps.name: Jarvis
apps.tagline: Your personal AI assistant — always in your pocket.
apps.description: Jarvis is a personal AI assistant that remembers your context, uses real tools instead of guessing, and manages your hosted sites and blogs through plain conversation. It runs against your own cloud, so your history stays yours.

features.title: Persistent memory
features.detail: Remembers context across sessions so you never have to repeat yourself.

features.title: Real tool use
features.detail: Searches the web, reads files, and runs actions — not just a chatbot.

features.title: Hosted sites & blogs
features.detail: Create, edit, and publish personal sites and blogs through conversation.

features.title: Private by default
features.detail: Your data stays in your own cloud, with no third-party storage in between.

features.title: In-app updates
features.detail: Checks this store on launch and installs new builds without a visit to the browser.

features.title: Open source
features.detail: The full stack is public and self-hostable if you want to run your own.

builds.requirements: Android 8.0 or newer, roughly 150 MB free space
install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Launch Jarvis, sign in, and start a conversation.

apps.name: ReWeb
apps.tagline: A browser that keeps old phones on the modern web.
apps.description: ReWeb is a lightweight browser for Android phones the rest of the web has left behind. It runs on the device's own system WebView, which the Play Store still updates independently of the OS, so a handset from 2016 can render today's sites. Where something genuinely cannot work, ReWeb says so and explains why instead of showing a blank page.

features.title: Built for old hardware
features.detail: Caps live tabs to what the device's memory allows, suspending the rest without losing them.

features.title: Honest diagnostics
features.detail: Runs real capability probes in your engine and reports PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN — never a guess.

features.title: Repairs old TLS
features.detail: Detects a frozen certificate store and shows how to install the modern root that fixes it.

features.title: Per-site user agents
features.detail: Switch a single site between mobile, desktop or a custom identity when it refuses your engine.

features.title: Installable web apps
features.detail: Save a site to run in its own window and its own task, with its own user agent.

features.title: Local by default
features.detail: No account, no sync, no server. History, bookmarks and downloads never leave the device.

install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Launch ReWeb, then open Diagnostics to see what your device's engine supports.

apps.name: Store
apps.tagline: Every app in the ecosystem, searchable, installable, and kept up to date.
apps.description: Store is the on-device front for this catalogue: it lists every app the Harith Kavish ecosystem ships, checks what you actually have installed against what's current, and installs or updates any of them — including itself — without a trip back to the browser.

features.title: Search the catalogue
features.detail: Find any ecosystem app by name, tagline, or category without leaving the app.

features.title: Real install status
features.detail: Checks the version actually installed on your phone, not just what you last downloaded.

features.title: Update everything
features.detail: Update any app — or all of them at once — from one screen.

features.title: Covers new apps automatically
features.detail: Any app added to this catalogue shows up here with no update to Store itself.

features.title: Self-updating
features.detail: Checks this store on launch and installs new builds of itself the same way it updates everything else.

features.title: Open source
features.detail: The full stack is public and self-hostable if you want to run your own.

install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Launch Store to browse, search, and update every app in the ecosystem.

apps.name: Music
apps.tagline: Your phone's music, album by album, and the newest releases in your languages.
apps.description: Music lists the audio on your phone album by album, with artwork borrowed from a shared catalogue when your files carry none. Discover shows the newest albums and singles in the languages you choose, film soundtracks among them, with the people behind them. It plays through the music apps you already have: connect your own Spotify and songs start on your account, with a now-playing bar, a queue and lock-screen controls.

features.title: Your library, by album
features.detail: Every album on the phone, as a grid or a list, with folders you can switch off.

features.title: Discover new releases
features.detail: This week's and this month's albums and singles in your languages, plus independent releases by genre.

features.title: Plays where you listen
features.detail: Hands each song to Spotify, YouTube Music or Apple Music, whichever is installed.

features.title: Your own Spotify
features.detail: Connect your account in Settings and songs play outright, with lock-screen controls.

features.title: Films and the people in them
features.detail: Soundtracks linked to their films, composers, cast and crew.

features.title: Sings along with Gallery
features.detail: Gallery's 3D face follows the song that is playing.

install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Launch Music and allow it to read your audio files.

apps.name: Gallery
apps.tagline: Your photos and videos, the people in them, and OneDrive alongside.
apps.description: Gallery shows every photo and video on your phone, newest first, with an Albums view of every folder and a storage breakdown on top. The People tab groups photos by who is in them, worked out on the phone with nothing uploaded. Sign in to OneDrive and those photos sit alongside your own. Deletes go to a recycle bin first, so nothing is lost by a slip.

features.title: Every photo and video
features.detail: Newest first under a heading per day, with zoom, swipe and video playback.

features.title: Albums and storage
features.detail: Every folder as a card, with what your images, GIFs and videos take up.

features.title: People, on the phone
features.detail: Faces are grouped on the device itself. No photo leaves it.

features.title: OneDrive alongside
features.detail: Your OneDrive photos in the same gallery, marked so you know where each lives.

features.title: Recycle bins
features.detail: Deleted files wait 30 days in the app's own bin, or OneDrive's, before they go.

features.title: A face that sings
features.detail: A 3D face that lip-syncs to whatever Music is playing.

install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Launch Gallery and allow it to read your photos and videos.

apps.name: Glass Keyboard
apps.tagline: A QWERTY keyboard you can see straight through.
apps.description: Glass Keyboard has no background of its own: the app behind shows through, and the keys read as panes of glass over whatever you are reading. It suggests and completes words, corrects typos and learns when you overrule it, and has a searchable emoji picker. It has no libraries at all and installs in a few hundred kilobytes. It asks for no permissions and makes no connections, so what you type stays in the app you typed it into.

features.title: Transparent by design
features.detail: No panel behind the keys: the app you are using stays visible while you type.

features.title: Suggestions and autocorrect
features.detail: Three suggestions as you type, and corrections that learn from being undone.

features.title: Emoji, searchable
features.detail: A picker by category, with search and your recent emoji.

features.title: Tints to your wallpaper
features.detail: Light or dark glass, chosen from your wallpaper, with an opacity slider.

features.title: Tiny
features.detail: No AndroidX, no Kotlin, no libraries. The whole app is a few hundred kilobytes.

features.title: No network, no account
features.detail: No permissions, no connections. Nothing you type leaves the device.

install: Open this page on your Android device and tap Get.
Allow installs from your browser under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps.
Open the downloaded file from your notification tray or Downloads folder and tap Install.
Open Glass Keyboard, turn it on under Languages and input, and pick it as your keyboard.
